svg.text: Test setup for step 3. The top + rail (5 V) comes from the Nucleo 5V pin (R1) on USB alone, or from the XL4015 (circuit 7).
USB cable to the laptop (power and code)
pins in row j, columns 42 to 47,
card slot over the top edge
Check the pin names printed on your board
Column map of the whole feeder:
Card: 8 to 32 GB, known brand, FAT32
Format it on the computer before first use
SPI1, mode 0; start at about 350 kHz,
then about 11 MHz (lower it if errors appear)
Module VCC on 5 V: it makes the 3.3 V itself
PA7 is not used: Ethernet needs it
1. Wire everything with the USB unplugged.
2. Insert or remove the card only with power off.
3. Keep the SPI wires short and together.
4. The card holds clips, schedule and logs.
5. Read errors: check GND first, then lower speed.
6. Check every Nucleo pin label before plugging.
Kibbly hardware · circuit 9 of the circuits by part · wires S1 to S6 in hardware/04_wiring_list.md section 10, rails R1, R3 and R4 in section 4B
